info.description:
Astro Agents — verifiable celestial & market-timing data for traders, quants and AI agents. Exact planetary positions (geocentric & heliocentric), declination, Gann planetary lines, planetary cycles and a to-the-minute celestial event calendar (ingresses, stations, eclipses) from the real NASA/JPL DE440 ephemeris — no LLM, every result reproducible and SHA-256 verifiable, so you can backtest and cite with no second-guessing. Pay per call natively in MCP with x402 (USDC on Base or Solana): zero setup, no account; or over REST (x402/MPP) or with prepaid credit packs. Full Western & Vedic astrology too (natal, kundli, dashas, KP, yogas). Data for your own analysis — never a trading signal or forecast.

Pay per call with **x402** (USDC on Base or Solana) or **MPP** (Tempo: OUSD or USDC.e). No account, no API key. 1 free call per client on the $0.01-0.02 routes, over REST, MCP or A2A; every other route, finance included, is always paid.

Official Python client: `pip install "astro-agents @ git+https://github.com/aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-clients#subdirectory=python"` (https://github.com/aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-clients/tree/main/python#readme).

- Positions from NASA/JPL DE440 (NASA/JPL), 1800-01-01..2200-01-01, via Skyfield: geocentric apparent, true equinox of date, IAU 2006/2000A.
- Historical time zones resolved for you (IANA tz database, DST of the era, Local Mean Time); ambiguous or non-existent local times are flagged, never guessed.
- Deterministic, no LLM: same input -> same bytes. Every response carries meta.input_sha256 and meta.result_sha256 (also as X-Input-SHA256 / X-Result-SHA256 headers); POST /v1/verify recomputes one.
- Every convention is in the response: ayanamsa (name, true and mean value), house system, orbs, node type, dasha year length, dosha and koota rule sets.
- Cross-validated against an independent engine (XALEN, Apache-2.0): ayanamsas agree to < 0.1", 15/16 divisional charts identically, all 11 house systems in structure.
- Accuracy vs NASA/JPL Horizons (12,400 comparisons, 1800-2199): positions within 0.024" (ICRF); ecliptic longitudes as served within 0.062" over 1962-2026. Method and every number: https://astro-agent.dev/benchmark.md

Pay per call with x402 (USDC on Base or Solana) or MPP, or inside MCP at /mcp. Data for your own analysis, never a signal or forecast. Astrology charts too: every chart endpoint takes a JSON body with a local 'datetime' (e.g. '1990-05-15T14:30'), 'latitude' and 'longitude'; the historical time zone is resolved for you. Cheapest calls: POST /v1/western/positions ($0.01) and /v1/vedic/nakshatra ($0.02). Western natal chart: POST /v1/western/natal. Vedic birth chart: POST /v1/vedic/kundli. Marriage compatibility: POST /v1/vedic/gun-milan with person_a and person_b. Each response carries meta.result_sha256; POST /v1/verify recomputes it. 1 free call per client on the $0.01-0.02 routes. Free catalog: GET /v1/catalog. /v1/finance/analogues also takes reference {birth: {datetime, latitude, longitude}} to compare a birth sky to past/future dates, data only. Crypto tokens: /v1/finance/token-chart (a token's launch sky and the key astronomical dates ahead, with an SVG card) and /v1/finance/token-synastry (two launch skies compared by geometry, with an SVG card).

post.description:
Planet degrees (geocentric and heliocentric) at a moment or as a time series, with aspect offsets, Mean of 5 / Circle of 8 and price levels.

Financial-astrology DATA for charting and backtests, not signals: the longitude of each planet, seen from the Earth and from the Sun in one call, plus the aspect offsets you ask for (+/-90, 120...), the Optuma averages Mean of 5 and Circle of 8, speeds, retrograde flags and declinations. Snapshot ('datetime') or series ('start', 'end', 'interval' 1h..1w, up to 1000 samples, optionally unwrapped for plotting) in columns ready for pandas. With 'price_unit' and 'price_range': every price level (degree + 360 k) x unit. Each result is hashed, so a backtest can cite and replay it.

datetime.description: A moment (snapshot): ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00Z'. A local time needs 'timezone' or coordinates. Omit when giving start/end.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

start.description: Series: first UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: '2024-01-01'.

end.description: Series: last UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 1000 samples).

interval.description: Series sampling step, in candle-timeframe notation.

time_utc.description: Series: UTC time of day of the first sample, HH:MM.

perspective.description: Geocentric, heliocentric, or both in one call (default).

bodies.description: Bodies to draw. Default: Sun..Pluto (geo), Mercury..Pluto with Earth (helio).

aspects.description: Aspect offsets added to every line (+angle and -angle). Default: the planet's own line only (conjunction).

averages.description: Optuma averages: mean_of_5 = (Jupiter+Saturn+Uranus+Neptune+Pluto)/5, circle_of_8 = (Mercury..Pluto)/8, in each perspective.

average_method.description: 'arithmetic' mean of the 0-360 longitudes (Optuma's rule) or 'circular' (vector) mean.

price_unit.description: Price per degree. With price_range: levels = (degree + 360 k) x price_unit.

price_range.description: The price window in which to list levels, e.g. {min: 30000, max: 80000}.

unwrap.description: Series: continuous degrees (no 360 -> 0 jump), for plotting lines across a chart.

include_declination.description: Series: also a declination column per body.

format.description: Series layout: 'columns' (pandas.DataFrame(result['series'])) or 'rows' (one object per sample).

frames.geocentric: geocentric apparent, true ecliptic and equinox of date
frames.heliocentric: heliocentric geometric positions (Sun -> body, no light-time), true ecliptic and equinox of date

settings.line_id: <geo|helio>.<body or average>[+<offset deg>]; degree = (longitude + offset) mod 360
settings.price_formula: price = (degree + 360 k) x price_unit, for every integer k in price_range

post.description:
Eclipse and Mercury retrograde calendar: every solar and lunar eclipse, station (retrograde/direct), ingress, new and full moon, aspect, parallel and out-of-bounds between two dates (1800-2200), to the minute.

A reproducible calendar of celestial events for backtests and alerts, historical or future: sign ingresses, retrograde/direct stations, new/full/quarter moons, solar eclipses (total, annular, hybrid, partial, with gamma) and lunar eclipses (with magnitudes), aspects between planets, declination parallels / contra-parallels and out-of-bounds crossings. Up to 366 days per call, geocentric or heliocentric, tropical or sidereal, Moon optional. Each event has exact_utc, a unix 'timestamp' to join on candle times and a stable 'key' for de-duplication across pages.

post.description:
Find the past or future dates whose planetary positions best match a reference sky, ranked by a stated angular distance.

Matching skies by geometry, data only: give a reference (a UTC moment, 'now', your own positions, or a birth sky: compare a birth sky to past/future dates — data only) and get the dates in a range (past, future or both, 1800-2200, 1h..1w grid) whose sky is closest, ranked by a weighted mean of circular longitude differences (geocentric and/or heliocentric), pair angles (aspects), declination differences and retrograde-flag mismatches, in degrees. Each match gives its date, unix timestamp, score, every body's exact longitude and retrograde flag and each feature's distance, in columns ready for pandas. The metric formula is in the response; the same request returns the same bytes and hash, future dates included. Up to 100 matches and 36,600 candidate dates per call; no market data. Data for your own analysis — never a signal or forecast.

reference.description: The sky to match: 'now' (default; the current UTC hour or day, echoed in result.reference.date_utc), a UTC moment ('2026-10-29T00:00Z' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'), {datetime: ...}, your own configuration {values: {feature id: value}} (add 'datetime' to anchor direction and range at a time), or a birth sky {birth: {datetime: local '1990-05-15T14:30', latitude, longitude, timezone?}} to compare a birth sky to past/future dates. The birth moment is resolved as in /v1/western/positions (time zone from the coordinates or 'timezone'); a date alone means 12:00 local with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning (the Moon is then approximate, Jupiter..Pluto stay reliable). No houses or ascendant. meta.reference_resolution gives the equivalent {values, datetime} request, which returns the same result and result_sha256. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde' (true/false).

datetime.description: Local birth time, e.g. '1990-05-15T14:30', or the date alone if the time is unknown.

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Europe/Paris'; optional with latitude/longitude or an offset in datetime.

direction.description: Search before the reference (a birth: before the birth moment), after it, or both (default; the only choice with reference.values without 'datetime').

range.description: Candidate dates. Default (a reference with a time): the longest window the caps allow, up to 100 years in the chosen direction (50 on each side for 'both').

resolution.description: Step of the candidate grid. At most 36,600 candidate dates per call, and at most 660,000 dates x ephemeris series (one per body and perspective, plus one per retrograde-flagged body).

perspective.description: Positions seen from the Earth, from the Sun, or both.

bodies.description: Bodies to match. Default: Sun..Pluto (geo), Mercury..Pluto with Earth (helio).

features.description: What to compare: 'longitude' (default), 'aspects' (the angle between every pair of bodies), 'declination', 'retrograde' (geocentric flags, Mercury..Pluto).

weights.description: Optional {feature id: weight}, default 1 each, e.g. {'geo.jupiter': 2}. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde' (true/false).

max_distance.description: Optional: only matches whose score (degrees) is at most this.

min_separation_days.description: Minimum gap between two matches and between a match and the reference time, so one passage gives one match. Raise it (e.g. 3650) to skip the current cycle of slow planets.

require_same_retrograde.description: Keep only dates whose retrograde flags equal the reference's.

metric.score: score = sum(w_i * d_i) / sum(w_i) over the matched features i, in degrees; 0 = the same sky
metric.circular_difference: circ(a, b) = |((a - b + 180) mod 360) - 180|, in [0, 180] (mod with a non-negative result)
metric.aspects: feature '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle': angle = circ(longitude_a, longitude_b), in [0, 180]; d = |angle_reference - angle_candidate|
metric.retrograde: feature 'geo.<body>:retrograde' (retrograde = geocentric longitude speed < 0): d = 0 if the flag equals the reference's, else 180
metric.weights: w_i = 1 unless 'weights' {feature id: w >= 0} says otherwise
metric.selection: eligible candidates (direction; at least min_separation_days from the reference time; score <= max_distance; the reference's retrograde flags if require_same_retrograde) are ordered by (score rounded to 1e-9, timestamp), and each is kept if it lies at least min_separation_days from every match already kept, until top_n are kept
metric.values: positions on the candidate grid from DE440 via Skyfield with IAU 2000B nutation, as in the planetary-lines series; the score is computed before the response rounds values to 1e-6

frames.geocentric: geocentric apparent, true ecliptic and equinox of date; declinations on the true equator of date
frames.heliocentric: heliocentric geometric positions (Sun -> body, no light-time), true ecliptic and equinox of date

settings.columns: rank, date_utc, timestamp (unix s), days_from_reference, score (degrees), each body's longitude '<geo|helio>.<body>', 'geo.<body>:retrograde', the matched angle and declination values, and 'distance:<feature id>' (degrees)
settings.note: Matching skies by a stated angular distance, no market data. Data for your own analysis — never a signal or forecast.

post.description:
Launch sky of a token: planet positions, retrogrades and aspects at its launch moment, plus the key astronomical dates ahead (exact returns and aspects to those positions), with a shareable SVG card.

Give a token's launch moment (the block time of its contract deployment or mint, UTC, to the second) and get the geocentric sky at that instant: each planet's sign, degree, longitude and retrograde flag, the major aspects between them, element and modality balance (no houses: a token has no place). Then the key dates: the exact UTC minute, over up to 366 days from 'from', at which each transiting planet returns to its launch position or aspects a launch position, each with a unix timestamp and a stable key, in rows ready for pandas. result.card.svg is a server-rendered 1200x675 card (wheel, positions, next key dates) ready to post. Key astronomical dates, data only — never a signal or forecast.

launch_datetime.description: The token's launch moment in UTC: ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, to the second ('2018-08-03T19:28:24Z'), or unix seconds (an on-chain block time). Use the block time of the contract deployment or of the mint, from an explorer.

address.description: Contract or mint address (shown on the card).

symbol.description: Ticker shown on the card, e.g. 'USDC'.

name.description: Name shown on the card, e.g. 'USD Coin'.

token.description: Optional label drawn on the card and echoed in the result. On-chain resolution of the launch time is not available yet: give launch_datetime.

from.description: First UTC date of the key dates, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today (UTC); pass it for a reproducible call. Example: '2026-11-01'.

days.description: How many days of key dates from 'from'.

transit_bodies.description: Transiting bodies timed against the launch positions (default all nine).

limit.description: Maximum key dates returned (counts.key_dates gives the total).

orbs.description: Orb overrides in degrees per aspect, e.g. {'conjunction': 6}.

post.description:
Compatibility by sky geometry of two tokens: the cross-aspects between their launch skies, harmonious and tense counts, the tightest aspects and a geometry score, with a shareable SVG card.

Two launch moments (UTC block times) compared like a synastry, without houses: every major cross-aspect between token A's and token B's planets with its orb and exactness, harmonious (trine, sextile) / tense (square, opposition) / conjunction counts, the five tightest aspects as readable labels, and geometry_score = 100 x H / (H + T) where H and T sum the exactness (1 - orb / orb allowed) of harmonious and tense aspects -- an aggregate of geometry, defined in the response, not a rating. Next to it, 'substance' says how much geometry the score stands on: aspects_total, counts (harmonious, tense, conjunction), tight_aspects (orb <= 1 deg), the tightest aspect with its orb, the orb threshold, the summed exactness and a confidence label by tight aspects (rich >= 7, moderate 3-6, thin <= 2; the rule is in the response). Rows ready for pandas; result.card.svg is a server-rendered card naming both tokens, with the substance under the score. Data only — never a signal or forecast.

post.description:
Planetary positions for any date and time (ephemeris): tropical or sidereal longitude, latitude, speed and retrograde flag of the Sun, Moon, Mercury..Pluto, nodes and Lilith.

Geocentric apparent positions from NASA/JPL DE440 for any moment 1800-2200, with sign, degree, element, modality, daily speed and retrograde status. Location is optional (only used to interpret a local time). Options: perspective 'heliocentric' (seen from the Sun) and coordinates 'equatorial' (right ascension, declination, out-of-bounds).

datetime.description: Local birth date-time, ISO 8601: '1990-05-15T14:30' (local clock time at the place) or with an explicit offset '1990-05-15T14:30:00+02:00'. Alternative: 'date' + 'time'.

time.description: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, 24 h. Omit if unknown (computed at 12:00 with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning).

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

post.summary: Sky today: retrogrades, Moon phase, next events ($0.01)
post.description:
The sky today (no birth data): planet positions, retrogrades and Moon phase now, plus the exact UTC times of the next ingresses, stations (Mercury retrograde), new and full moons and aspects.

For agents and bots that follow the sky itself (market timing, daily content, alerts): positions with retrograde flags and the Moon's phase and illumination at a moment (default: now, UTC), then every sign ingress, retrograde/direct station, lunation (new, quarter, full) and major aspect between the planets over the next 1-90 days, each to the minute. Tropical or sidereal. Pass 'datetime' for a reproducible call.

datetime.description: Local birth date-time, ISO 8601: '1990-05-15T14:30' (local clock time at the place) or with an explicit offset '1990-05-15T14:30:00+02:00'. Alternative: 'date' + 'time'.

time.description: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, 24 h. Omit if unknown (computed at 12:00 with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning).

timezone.description: IANA zone, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'. Optional: resolved from the coordinates, with the historical offset (DST, Local Mean Time) of that date.

time_basis.description: What the given clock time is: civil wall-clock (default), UTC, Local Mean Time, or true (apparent) solar time.

days.description: How many days ahead to list events. Example: 30.

schema.description: All optional: the moment (default now, UTC). A local time needs a timezone or coordinates.

settings.precision: event times +/- 1 minute (UTC); sidereal ingresses of slow planets +/- a few minutes (ayanamsa interpolated across the window)

post.description:
Aspects (with orb, exactness, applying/separating) for a moment, or for any longitudes you supply.

Either give a moment (datetime, optional place) and get the aspects among all planets, or give 'longitudes' {name: degrees} and get the pure geometry. Orbs are explicit and overridable. With options.declination: declinations and the parallels / contra-parallels too.
